blocks.text: The labour market continues its gradual cooling. Job openings have fallen from their peak, hiring has slowed and wage growth is moderating, yet layoffs remain low by historical standards.

Slower wage growth matters most for labour-intensive services, where pay is the largest cost. A continued gentle slowdown would do much of the remaining work on core inflation without requiring a sharp rise in unemployment.

items: Participation has stabilised after earlier gains.
Hours worked offer an early signal of softening demand.
Sectors with the strongest post-pandemic hiring are now normalising fastest.

blocks.text: A soft landing depends on the labour market bending rather than breaking. So far, the data is consistent with that path.
